summary: Test changes in commit d6037b0 implement Scenarios A-H from the tech-spec Testing Strategy and lock AC-1..AC-8 with deterministic, behaviour-focused unit tests. All resolver branches (Boolean.TRUE / Boolean.FALSE / absent) are covered with non-vacuous assertions; cookie-flag pass-through is asserted per attribute (not as a single all-defaults check); the re-login flip test exercises two independent exchanges to prove the resolver is stateless across requests; logout via expireSession is asserted regardless of the rememberMe attribute. AuthServiceTest extensions assert the exchange attribute is actually written in both login branches by reading back through a real ConcurrentHashMap, and the new register_autoLogin test explicitly locks Boolean.FALSE (not 'absent') as required by AC-6. Litmus test passes for every behavioural assertion: removing the production-side branch (the .maxAge() call in the resolver, or the exchange.getAttributes().put in AuthService.openSession) makes the corresponding test fail. Test names in RememberMeWebSessionIdResolverTest and AuthServiceTest match the TDD Anchor list in tasks/1.md verbatim. The unrelated AuthServiceRegistrationTest fix (verify name=null on the verification email) is correct and consistent with the prior name-removal commit. No critical or major findings; one minor observation noted.

findings.title: Scenario F secure pass-through covers only false→true flip
findings.detail: setSessionId_secure_passThroughFromConfig sets cookieProps.secure=true on top of propsWithDefaults() (which sets secure=false) and asserts cookie.isSecure()==true. The other direction is not asserted explicitly — i.e. there is no test that sets cookieProps.secure=false on a request whose URI scheme is https, to prove that the configured 'false' wins over the seeded https-default 'true'. The current production code uses .secure(scheme==https) as a seed and then PropertyMapper.alwaysApplyingWhenNonNull overrides; if a future refactor accidentally drops the override on this attribute (e.g. only mapping when the prop differs from the seed), the false→true flip test would still pass while the true→false direction would silently regress. This is the only Scenario F attribute where the seed default is request-derived rather than constant, so the asymmetry matters more here than for path/domain/sameSite.
findings.suggestion: Add a small companion test setSessionId_secure_explicitFalseWinsOverHttpsScheme: build the exchange via MockServerHttpRequest.post(URI.create("https://localhost/api/auth/login")) (so the seed is secure=true), set cookieProps.setSecure(false), call setSessionId, assert cookie.isSecure() is false. Confirms the PropertyMapper override path actively flows through both directions. Optional — the existing test plus AC coverage in pre-deploy QA already catches the practical regression.
